title: Memory spool backend: a contract that is partly infeasible
description: Type L (replan without scope expansion). The task asks for a memory backend with 'the same public contract' as the file backend — but the file reader's contract includes read_from(byte_offset)/offset_of_last() with BYTE offsets that callers persist between polls. A memory backend cannot honor byte offsets as-is: the route as specified is partly infeasible. Good plans discover this at planning time and pre-declare a LEGAL replan action from the closed set (replace_route — e.g. a logical-offset adapter — or reduce_scope — memory backend implements the subset with an explicit, documented deviation). Anti-plans: silently changing the file contract, pretending byte offsets work on a list, or expanding scope (ring buffer, compaction, replication, a 'real' queue service).
